edits.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu: Shall we say that Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that consecrated animals are disqualified and are no longer fit for sacrifice after they have been disqualified once?

Shall we say Rabbi Yochanan holds, etc.: From the fact that we needed to answer according to him concerning one who designates an offering after midday, it indicates that if one had not heard from him that living animals are permanently disqualified, it would be fitting to designate them forever. For perhaps disqualification applies only to slaughtered animals, as in the case of the scapegoat whose blood is poured out, as discussed in Tractate Yoma (62b).
